title: Which rotating arm passes through the slit?
description: One rotating arm is traced on cardboard and cut out as a slit. All the arms are mixed up, and each is placed over the slit to see which one passes. Keeko's doubt is that the arm with the smaller angle passes because it is thinner.
teaching_notes: One idea: an arm passes through the slit only when its angle is equal to the slit's angle. Watch for students who think a smaller angle fits more easily.

source: Collect a number of rotating arms with different angles (do
video_script.why: The child finds which rotating arm fits a slit by placing each arm over it.
video_script.substitution: the book's own cardboard slit and the rotating arms
video_script.anchor: a cardboard with an angle-shaped slit and several rotating arms beside it
video_script.wrong_answer: the arm with the smaller angle goes through
video_script.wrong_move: thinks a thinner arm slips through any slit
video_script.payoff_line: Only the arm whose angle is equal to the slit passes through

final_answer.value: only the arm whose angle is equal to the slit's angle passes through; place each arm over the slit to find it
final_answer.spoken: only the arm whose angle is equal to the slit passes through, so place each arm over the slit to find it

hold_back: angle is equal to the slit
maths_rules: trace one rotating arm on cardboard and cut out its shape; this is the slit
do not rotate any arm during the activity
slit angle greater than the arm's angle: the arm does not go through
slit angle less than the arm's angle: the arm does not go through
slit angle equal to the arm's angle: the arm goes through
passing through depends only on the angle, not on the lengths of the straws, as long as they are shorter than the slit
video_script.design: One idea: only an arm with an angle equal to the slit passes through. The cardboard and the arms stay on the board. Keeko's doubt: the arm with the smaller angle goes through.

<bookmark mark='cut'/>Trace one arm on the cardboard, and cut out its shape. This cut-out is called a slit.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>Mix up all the arms. Can you tell which arm will pass through the slit?

<bookmark mark='arm'/>An arm goes through only if its straws fit between the edges.

narration: <bookmark mark='greater'/>Step two, look at the gaps. If the slit angle is greater than the arm, the arm does not go through.

narration: <bookmark mark='equal'/>Step four, if the two angles are exactly equal, both straws touch both edges. Then the arm goes through.

narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>Only the arm whose angle is equal to the slit passes through.
